topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic origins and conditions of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can produce cancer through clonal evolution when cellular circumstances permit their accumulation and outgrowth.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk rather than cancer being attributable simply to chance or inherited predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the connection between infection and malignant transformation.

topics.label: Environmental exposures and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage capable of generating cancer-associated mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutational initiation from the promotional conditions that allow initiated cells to proliferate into tumours.

topics.label: Tissue susceptibility and recap of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics conclude the account of carcinogenic mechanisms by explaining tissue susceptibility and placing it within the preceding causal framework.

topics.label: Mutational signatures as evidence of carcinogen exposure
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how patterns in cancer genomes can reveal evidence of exposure to particular carcinogens.

topics.label: Methods and limitations of carcinogenicity assessment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the available methods for establishing carcinogenic potential and the limitations of the evidence they produce.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by recapping its main conclusions and framing their relevance to everyday risk–benefit decisions.
